articles.title: Grab Philips Shavers at a Steep Discount at Amazon Right Now
articles.summary: Save hundreds on Philips Shavers, including the Prestige Ultra model which is now better than half price.
articles.body:
If you’ve never used an electric shaver, you really are missing out. They’re smooth, they’re satisfying, and quite often they’ll net you a closer shave than a manual razor that gets duller in days.

Thankfully, Philips has an array of excellent options, and they’re seeing decent discounts right now at Amazon - including a whopping 51% off the i9000 Prestige Ultra, which sounds like it should be a car rather than something you use on your face.

We’ve already pointed out the OneBlade is seeing a great discount, but it’s not alone in that regard - and there’s something for just about any budget right now with these discounts at Amazon.

Take the Philips Electric Shaver Series 3000X , for example. It’s a sleek, comfortable device that would usually set you back £54.99, now just £44.99.

Not the biggest discount, admittedly, but for a first electric razor it’s really hard to go wrong. It offers a comfortable, clean shave that won’t leave marks despite using 27 self-sharpening blades, and is guaranteed for two years.

Those blades cup up to 55,000 times per minute to keep your shave steady and consistent, and the three heads can flex in four directions to match the contours of your face.

Next up is the Philips Electric Shaver Series 5000 , which, again, has 27 self-sharpening blades as well as a clip-on trimmer to maintain your ‘tache, trim your sideburns, or shape up your eyebrows (if you’re feeling brave).

Unlike the aforementioned model, its heads move 360 degrees to help with comfort while shaving, plus there’s a display that shows when it needs cleaning, charging, or the heads need replacing. It’s now £74.99, down 53% from its RRP of £159.99.

Looking for something even fancier for your face? The Philips Shaver i9000 Prestige Ultra (you know it’s good because ‘Prestige’ and ‘Ultra’ are in the name) usually sells for £649.99 - you could buy a whole new face for that.

Still, it’s an Amazon Exclusive, award-winning shaver that has a seven-year warranty and offers a 20% more precise shave than a manual razor. Its 360 rotating blades are ideal for cutting hair in all directions, and it includes SkinIQ Pro technology, which helps recommend changes in pressure and direction as you shave. It’s now down to £319.99, marking a 51% discount on that eye-watering RRP.

Whether it’s a big social occasion, a job interview, or just everyday maintenance, it’s clear there’s never been a better time to pick up a new shaver and revitalise your look.

articles.title: Chess.com launched a poker site and is planning even more classic games
articles.summary: Chess.com’s new poker site, Gambit, is its first expansion, and now it’s working on launching sites for more games, like go, backgammon, and mahjong.
articles.body: Chess.com has done one thing, and one thing very well, for almost 20 years, but now it’s going beyond its domain name. The biggest name in online chess quietly launched its first companion site in beta back in May: Gambit, a free online poker website where players can learn the game without risking any real money. Now Gambit’s ready to really get the ball rolling with its first livestreamed event and collaborations with content creators, and Chess.com is planning to branch out into even more games from here. Chess.com’s chief growth officer, Albert Cheng, told The Verge the company chose poker for its first companion site because, like chess, it has learning and social elements on top of just playing the game. He also promised there will never be real-money gambling on Gambit, saying, “Real money is the problem we built Gambit to get away from, the whole industry makes money when beginners lose. We’d rather build a place where people can actually learn.” Gambit will look familiar to anyone who’s used Chess.com. It borrows the same design style and includes similar play modes, like bot matches, games with friends, tournaments, a review mode for studying your past games, and a learning mode. Gambit even includes Chess.com’s bot characters, with matching skill levels — I immediately recognized “Martin,” the lowest skill level bot from Chess.com, who is also the lowest skill level bot on Gambit. [Image: [Image: Chess.com also developed its own Elo-style rating system for Gambit. Cheng explained in an interview with The Verge that the rating system serves as the main motivator for players to improve: “You’re not gambling your own hard-earned money necessarily, so the stakes are lower from that standpoint, but you need something to counterbalance it that you care about, and that keeps the ecosystem in play, and keeps the poker that’s on Gambit reasonably high-quality.” The rating system is also the backbone of Gambit’s paid subscription for access to premium learning features, following the same model Chess.com uses. “Our primary business model of Chess.com is a subscription, but most people play Chess.com for free,” Cheng said. “They subscribe to get unlimited access to review their games and to get unlimited puzzles, lessons, et cetera.” A reliable rating system allows players to track their improvement, potentially motivating them to pay for those premium features. [Image: [Image: Rating systems are also at the heart of Chess’s next move. Chess.com is now looking to expand into even more classic games, including go, backgammon, and mahjong. Like Gambit, Chess.com is developing Elo-style rating systems for these games, as well. Cheng didn’t say when the new sites will launch but that “development is moving quite rapidly” on them, using the same playbook he used for Gambit. AI is a key reason Chess.com was finally able to expand into other games after nearly 20 years, according to Cheng. He and one other employee took Gambit from prototype to launch within a year, partly with help from AI, mainly for coding tasks. “I think the biggest advantage that it’s provided is essentially being able to read our existing codebase and our design system and apply consistent patterns to how we develop Chess.com over to a different platform and do so quickly,” Cheng said. He went on to add that there were also a lot of areas where AI struggles, such as brand and feature design. “I think that’s the best ultimate use of AI is that ultimately it’s going to be a blend, right?” Cheng said, adding, “Just because code is easier to write doesn’t mean that you just let it run on its own, but it certainly is a superpower in getting things off the ground.” Cheng also said the version of Gambit that’s live at the time of writing has “zero or close to zero” AI-created assets, which were used in early prototypes. According to Cheng, without help from AI, getting another site up and running would have required a bigger team or “would have been a lot more disruptive to the status quo of building and growing Chess.” Now that a “small, scrappy” team can get a new platform off the ground much faster, it’s opened the door for Chess.com to dip into more games, starting with poker. As Chess.com plans its next move, Cheng says they’re focusing on games with “both that classic durability plus the community around it,” like chess. Now that Gambit has launched, Cheng’s leaning into the community and social side of the platform more, following Chess.com’s lead, and getting content creators more involved. On August 31st at 12PM ET / 9AM PT, Gambit’s livestreaming its Gambit Cup for the first time on Twitch and YouTube with Chess.com co-founder Danny Rensch and chess content creator Alexandra Botez.

articles.title: PSA: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets a $50 Price Increase on Tuesday
articles.summary: Nintendo is raising the price of the Switch 2 to $500 on September 1, meaning this is your last chance to get one before the hike.
articles.body:
Compared to Sony and Microsoft , Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices. But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1. So, starting Tuesday, you’ll have to fork out $500 for a new hybrid console instead of the current MSRP of $450. In other words, if you’re thinking of picking up a Switch 2, this is your last chance to do so before the price hike.

When it comes to buying a Switch 2, you used to have more options than you do today. Previously, you could buy the console all by itself, or bundled with a game. There was even a bundle that let you choose among three first-party games. As we creep toward the price hike, however, all of the bundles have vanished from retailers. Your only reasonably priced option now is wither to buy a Switch 2 new or refurbished .

New Switch 2 consoles are available at all the usual retailers ( see at Amazon ). Refurbished Switch 2s are available at several retailers, but the best deal going right now is a “Grade A” refurbished unit at Woot for $399.99 . That’s $50 less than the current price of a new Switch 2, and it’s the best deal going if you don’t mind refurbished hardware.

Woot, by the way, is owned by Amazon, so you can rest assured it’s a legit retailer. I’ve bought many things from Woot and never had any problems.

Nintendo has announced it will introduce two new Switch 2 bundles after the price hike. One includes a copy of Mario Kart World . It will be available in “late September” and cost $549.99. The other includes Nintendo Switch Sports Resort . It will cost $529.99 and will be out October 22, the day that game comes out.

Both bundles will include three months of Nintendo Switch Online, and offer slight discounts versus buying the items individually. But neither bundle will save you more than $50, meaning your best bet is still to buy before the price goes up.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Everything Coming to Disney+ in September
articles.body:
Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Toy Story 5 are both making their way to Disney+ in September, where they'll be joined by new episodes of The Simpsons and plenty of Hulu Originals. The only slice of Disney that isn't seeing many streaming debuts this month is Marvel, but there's already plenty of homework to work through before Avengers: Doomsday .

Without further ado, here's everything new Disney+ subscribers are getting this month.

Everything Coming to Disney+ in September

Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro S1 (Finale)

Disney Jr. Ariel – The Little Mermaid S2 (New Episodes)

Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective Podcast

The Mina Kimes Show featuring Lenny Podcast

Disney+ is starting off September by crowning a winner in the new Dancing With the Stars spin-off, The Next Pro. Throughout the month, Disney+ will also be getting pretty much every episode from a selection of ESPN podcasts, starting with the The Mina Kimes Show and the Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective Podcast.

Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu Official Podcast (Two-Episode Premiere @ 9pm ET)

One of two particularly big movie premieres this month, Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu is landing on Disney+ after a pretty disappointing run at the box office. Our 5/10 review also wasn’t as positive as we’ve been about The Mandalorian TV series , but that doesn’t mean it isn’t worth checking out. Project Runway S22 (New Episode @ 10pm PT)

Disney+ recently re-acquired the streaming rights to Pokemon, and kicked things off by dropping the first 26 episodes of the original Indigo League series. I was confused about the somewhat random selection of episodes , but it looks like Disney+ is going to be adding the Pokemon series in batches.

Project Runway S22 – Final Episode @ 10pm PT

Dancing with the Stars Official Podcast – Premiere

MonsterQuest originally aired on the History Channel in the late 2000s and features some solid monster hunting of the era. And yes, Disney+ is getting yet another podcast, this time about and in the lead-up to the new season of Dancing With the Stars.

9/11 Tribute in Light: Live from Lower Manhattan – ABC News Live Special at 8pm ET

The aforementioned new season of Dancing With the Stars kicks off right in the middle of September, with new episodes livestreamed directly onto Disney+.

Minimum Security (All Episodes Streaming)

Unexpected Loves (All Episodes Streaming)

Disney+ will be livestreaming this year’s iHeartRadio music festival, featuring headliners like BTS, Cardi B, and Weezer. You can check out the full lineup here .

Dancing with the Stars S35 – Streaming Live at 8pm ET

The other big streaming premiere of the month, Toy Story 5, is landing on Disney+ after crossing $1 billion at the box office and becoming the highest-grossing Toy Story movie so far. articles.title: Every Cosmere Tabletop Game Based on Brandon Sanderson's Epic Book Universe
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson’s Cosmere universe has delighted readers ever since his first book, Elantris, released more than two decades ago. Now, it spans over 20 books with more in the works and even a new movie and television series looming based on the immensely popular Mistborn and Stormlight Archive books, respectively. Over the years, the tales of Vin, Kaladin, and the Shards of Adonalsium have made the jump from page to the tabletop as well, with a number of board games and tabletop roleplaying games having been released for players to enjoy.

This list showcases all of the tabletop games that you can currently experience, along with the ones that we know about!

Brotherwise Games , publishers of games like Boss Monster, Night of the Ninja, and Call to Adventure, this studio is the official partner for Sanderson’s Cosmere when it comes to the board game space. So far they have released a solid mix of titles with something for nearly all ages of Cosmere fans, with some of their biggest stuff still on the way.

Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive

Built on Brotherwises’ “Call to Adventure” board game system, Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive asks players to create the most epic and interesting character they can. A bit of an engine builder, you will be drafting cards to build out your character's history, motivation, and destiny while balancing their morality, all culminating at the end in your own personal hero’s journey and scoring points. Complete quests by rolling nifty rune slabs, balance on the thin line between hero and anti-hero through three rounds with the winner being whoever has the most dragic/awesome character backstory (aka has the most points). Not only can CtA: The Stormlight Archive is not only a solid game, but also a great character-building exercise which is perfect for the next game…

Stormlight Handbook, Cosmere RPG Core Rulebook

Stormlight Archive Stonewalkers Adventure

For the tabletop roleplaying fans, the Cosmere RPG gives you the tools and systems to live out your dreams in the world of Roshar. Whether you want to walk down the path of becoming a knight radiant, take on the form of a singer, or perhaps just a simple soldier trying to survive, the Cosmere RPG gives you the tools to do all that and more. Your character’s motivation and the story you and your friends create in the Cosmere are the driving force behind this system and Brotherwise is just getting started with the world of Scadrail and its Allomancers coming soon as well. A host of products are available, from the Stormlight Handbook with all you need to run a campaign on Roshar, the Stonewalkers Adventure for a constructed story, and even a welcoming Starter Set if you just want to get a taste.

Showcasing events and characters from the first book of the Mistborn series, The Final Empire, the Mistborn: The Deckbuilding Game puts 1-4 players in the roles of beloved characters including Vin and Kelsier. Players will build out their decks from an available pull of cards while also learning and improving their ability to burn metals as allomancers - the signature magic of the world of Scadriel. All the while, working to become strong enough to complete missions and take out the other players, or the Lord Ruler himself in an optional cooperative game mode. With gorgeous artwork and solid deckbuilding at its core, this game is a great buy for fans of Mistborn, and it will be getting an expansion soon as well, that adds new characters, powers, and highlight moments from the second book, the Well of Ascension!

The lightest of the main three Cosmere games from Brotherwise, Shards of Creation is a ticktaking card game where depending on which of the Shards of Adonalsium get picked can greatly change how you play. Each of the Shards included in the base game: Autonomy, Cultivation, Devotion, Dominion, Honor, Odium, Preservation and Ruin feature unique powers that can both help or hurt you as you form sets of suits for end game scoring. Featuring canonical depictions of the vessels of the Shards (up to a point, anyway), some of which first appearing in Shards of Creation, make this a great option for both fans of the Cosmere but also folks who just enjoy a good trick-taking game to bust out when they have a little time on their hands.

Prior to Brotherwise securing their partnership with Sanderson, another group, publisher Crafty Games, had a go adapting the author’s popular Mistborn series for the tabletop.

Set during the first book, House War is a resource management game where as opposed to taking up the Mistcloak of a specific character, each player assumes the role of one of the factions around the city. The aim is to keep down the unrest by solving issues around the Empire, competing to earn the most favor. This game is less about burning metals and pushing through the mists and more about making deals, but House War has the twist where its possible the player with either the lowest or highest score could potentially win. There are also rules that allow shorter games to play out in 60-90 minutes or longer games between two and three hours long, give you and your group flexibility to slot this in either as a bit of a filler game or be the main game of the night. An expansion, “The Siege of Luthadel” expands the game and sets the game during the second novel and attempts to hold everything together.

The first TTRPG set in the world of the Cosmere, released first back in summer of 2012, this tabletop adventure system lets players build Nobels, Skaa, Terrismen and even Kandra in the world of Scadrial to live out their stories during the first era of the Mistborn saga. Developed by Crafty Games, this d6 based system is far more narrative-driven where factors like Destiny and Tragedy factor into character creation. There are a host of expansions and additional books that were released for MDA including Terris: Wrought of Copper that focuses on the Terris people and Feruchemists, Alloy of Law, Skaa: Tin & Ash, Alloy of Law: Masks of the past, and Nobels: The Golden Mandate.

If you are still hungry for more, Brotherwise Games should have you covered to get your Cosmere tabletop kick for some time yet, with a number of games and expansions on the horizon. The Mistborn deck builder has its first expansion, “ The Well of Ascension ,” featuring a new cooperative mode where players need to work together to defend the city of Luthadel from a horde of Koloss, and more pulled from the second book of era 2 Mistborn.

Staying on the Allomancer train, the Cosmere RPG will also soon be getting its Mistborn books , letting players create their own mistborns and allomancers while taking part in adventures set in both the first and second eras of the series!

Lastly, later this fall, Brotherwise will be bringing the Stormlight Archive to Kickstarter with their War for Roshar board game. Previously covered here on IGN with an exclusive preview , this is a heavy area control / euro title that will see up to four players facing off against either on the side of Honor or of Odium, struggling to capture Oathgates and turn the tide of the war in their favor.

Scott White is a freelance contributor to IGN, assisting with tabletop games and guide coverage. Follow him on X/Twitter or Bluesky .

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Think They Found Jason and Lucia's Vice City Apartment in Real Life
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself.

Grand Theft Auto players have proven time and time again that they will go to the ends of the earth to learn the smallest details about Rockstar Games experiences, and that hasn't changed for GTA 6. Just days after the big extended look presentation revealed Jason and Lucia's apartment in Vice City, one watcher took it upon themselves to hunt down what appears to be the same apartment in real-life Miami.

Instagram user prettyboycuh was the first to publicly share the location, saying they started by using Google Maps to find a tall teal building that was first shown in last week's gameplay trailer. They said "that was easy," but when they used the Street View function to turn to where Jason and Lucia's apartment should be, all they found was a patch of grass. Then, they turned back the clock.

They – and you can still see this for yourself, too – changed the map's time period from March 2026 to April 2013, around four months before the launch of GTA 5 , and voila, the apartment appeared. Rockstar hasn't officially confirmed what was known as the Belmar Condominium to be the inspiration for the spot we see Jason and Lucia hanging out at in GTA 6, but the similarities are too difficult to ignore. It's the same color, has the same fence, many of the buildings around it are the same, and we can even see the parking lot Jason pulled out of in the extended look. So, where'd it go?

IGN replicated prettyboycuh's findings and can report that the building stuck around through 2017 before it was repainted from its salmon color to some darker grays. It shows up on Google Maps through 2022 before a 2024 recording shows that the Miami location completely vanished.

prettyboycuh took things one step further and found a report from the South Florida Business Journal stating that The Belmar Condo was sold for a total of $12 million in 2022. The same report stated the building was established in 1973 before it was eventually demolished sometime after the buyout. In other words, if you're a GTA 6 fan looking to visit what could become one of the most recognizable locations in Jason and Lucia's story, you're out of luck.

Still, you can see the location through Google Maps to this day, and prettyboycuh discovered that Rockstar inadvertently gave fans more to gawk at, too. Archived Zillow listings show the developer was not only thorough when mapping the outside of the apartment but the inside, too. From the brief glimpses we see of Jason grabbing drinks from the fridge, watching TV, and failing to impress Lucia with his outfit choices, it looks like their apartment pretty closely matches the real-life inspiration.

GTA 6 gave fans about 27 minutes of in-game footage last Thursday, and if this is the length players are going to already, there's no telling what the community will be like when the game actually launches. Previously, fans have (incorrectly) looked to the stars for hints , while others have taken things a bit too far . We'll all be able to revisit Vice City when it launches November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Be sure to also learn about what GTA 6 won't have at launch and the streamer who believes Rockstar designed a character based on himself . IGN recently got to learn a lot about the new Grand Theft Auto, but you can check out just 99 of our favorite details here . Our preview and interview are both also available for those looking to learn more.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: NBA 2K27 from developer Visual Concepts is another effort in the series aimed at walking the tightrope between modern upgrades and catering to player feedback.
articles.body:
NBA 2K27 from developer Visual Concepts is another effort in the series aimed at walking the tightrope between modern upgrades and catering to player feedback.

It's a tough balance to seek, no doubt. Last year's game kept pushing things in realistic directions on and off the court, while also listening to player feedback when it comes to shot meters and specific systems.

This year? More of the same, in a good way, with a push to get more realistic-feeling things on the court and finer control over the many systems off it.

The best entry yet thing is starting to become a cliché, sure, but NBA 2K27 has a shot at it once more thanks to measured upgrades atop a strong foundation.

One glance says the gameplay in NBA 2K27 is a leap. There's obvious new cutoff angles and droves of more dynamic animations, at the hoop amid contact or otherwise.

The strive for freshness and realism this year takes a Shai Gilgeous-Alexander slant with the long-awaited inclusion of the step-through up-and-under, which adds a more dynamic option to the gameplay, for the ball-handler and defender alike.

Expanded dribbling customization was a must and makes the cut. Each of the nearly 30 movements can now be attached and arranged as players see fit. It's a deeper level of control than ever on this front, and a welcome one.

Something as seemingly small as layup tunings turns up big on the court, too. Auto adjustments to fit the situation seem more dynamic than ever and it's pretty clear that dunking logic, based on those involved and the physics of it all, got an upgrade.

Shooters get some love too. The strong rhythm shooting mechanic is back and tweaked for the better, with successful rhythm shots now strictly requiring greening the timing.

Defense gets some love too, not to worry.

There's a revamped shot contest system that gives players finer control over just how aggressive they try to attack each shot. The result helpfully shows up on a colored meter, revealing the quality of the contest.

New defensive cutoffs help those on the backpedal, too. They feel good and enable players to keep pace with the dizzying number of new possible dribbling combos coming at them on cuts to the hoop.

Both ends of the court benefit from the tweaked takeover system, which now zooms in on five areas: Shooting, Finishing, Playmaking, Defense, and Rebounding. These are now able to be activated individually. Tracking these via each meter and being able to trigger them when needed, if possible, is a nice bit of strategic depth and a skill gap.

Overall, there's a new weight to the on-court physics, too, when it comes to collisions. It's an exclamation on the whole thing. There's going to be an adjustment period for players, but the smooth pick-up-and-play base with big skill depth is a fun time.

Beyond simple star-likeness upgrades and the usual graphical horsepower stuff, where does a series like NBA 2K continue to evolve?

Updates in realism and variety, of course. Jersey updates, player updates and special attention to arenas and crowds shine in what remains one of the most immersive sports games out there.

The game deserves its flowers for freshening up The City, too, with REC games now featuring new environments. These new areas won't shock from a basketball game standpoint, but it's still cool to play some hoops on top of a roof with a nice view, right?

Really, there's lots of little presentation love thrown into each mode, when needed. The new MyCareer eras, for example, features true-to-era broadcasting and environments.

These are little things, but they add up to quite a lot. Improved player physics, dynamic crowds and the little details really create an authentic-looking project that takes smart creative liberties in the arcade-like streetball realm when it can, too.

Like those before it, NBA 2K27 keeps making solid pushes across a variety of game modes. MyPlayer, of course, remains king.

Many of the big changes in MyPlayer arrive in the initial builder itself. There's reworked badge progression that gives players finer control over the created character. Wiggle room for a balanced build is there, but players can also hyper-focus on one trait.

Also new within the builder is a synergy system that lets players tweak things to the point of surpassing badge max potential. A nice touch, as are badge loadouts, making it easier to swap entire badge configurations at will.

Over in MyCareer, what the game promises as double the length of last year's story now includes co-op. It also includes eras, complete with historically locked rosters.

A notable problem here, though, is there's no era-hopping. If players want to experiment, it seemingly requires starting a new character over with low stats. That would certainly seem to nudge players toward microtransactions to speed things up.

As for co-op in the mode, a player joins a friend via a fictional character introduced in the G League. Said teammate is customizable to an extent, and AI will control him if there's no co-op enabled. A nice touch for those who want it, if nothing else.

MyNBA feels like it has more depth than ever before, too, thanks to some modern-feeling tweaks. Players can move more assets than ever in up to four-team trades. They need to worry about contract buyouts, international prospects and a morale system that keeps tabs on things like friendships within the locker room.

City is now co-ed, which includes the usual bells and whistles of the mode like Park, Proving Grounds, The Theater and more.

A nice exclamation point on the whole package is the Crew HQ, which is exactly what it sounds like. Players now have a home hub for their crew, which nicely includes small things like half courts all the way on up to 5v5 courts.

Last year's highlight, Street Kings, returns in a big way. Up to three players still get to take on bosses across multiple courts, with the weekly tournament boasting a tense championship game by the end of the run.

MyWNBA and The W get some single-player love in the form of updated progression and attribute systems, including moving those around at will. There's something to be said for MyWNBA getting the full control of its own franchise mode, just like the MyNBA counterpart.

MyTeam returns many of the same trappings, but tacks on rotating multiplayer modes and a unified auction house. Doesn't sound like much, but tack on new card rarities and the onslaught of collecting, exchanging and upgrades amid a live-service list of game modes and, frankly, MyTeam could be its own separate release.

There's a lot to love here. Immersive ways to insert oneself into the NBA or WNBA are a blast, as are the in-depth franchise options or even card-collecting activities. Wrapping all of these up in different, hoops-based gameplay in smart ways is where 2K really excels.

This year's release runs well and has that eye-boggling number of options, sliders and assists to poke through. But it's the same story for the long list of microtransactions too, for better or worse.

This feels like one of the more meaningful upgrade passes the 2K series has seen in a long time.

Usually, it's easy to point at one game mode that didn't get a lot of love. But there's no maybe next year sport adage this time: Franchise and card modes are deeper than ever, the arcade and customizable stuff is a blast and really, any of the modes are now deep enough to be their own separate releases.

Kudos to NBA 2K27, really. There's only so many ways a sports game can fundamentally grow on a per-year basis. But this one is a good example of how to do it across an all-audiences experience.

If there were a year to not skip an annual sports release, NBA 2K27 is the new shining example.

articles.title: Fable's Main Quest Will Take About 20 Hours to Beat
articles.summary: Fable's main quest will take around 20 hours to beat, Playground Games has confirmed.
articles.body:
Fable 's main quest will take around 20 hours to beat, Playground Games has confirmed.

Associate game directors Will Kennedy and Craig Littler shared the estimated length for the 2027 fantasy RPG during a group Q&A attended by Polygon at gamescom 2026. While the Xbox and Playground say Fable will have plenty of content to keep players busy for as long as they want, players won't be sinking hundreds of hours into the main story just to reach the credits.

"We have around 15-20 hours of mainline quest gameplay, we have around 15-20 of side and open-world exploration content gameplay," Kennedy said.

As sprawling RPGs have continued to fill the space, that might come up a bit short for what some players were expecting. Open-world games like Elden Ring , The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , and Assassin's Creed Valhalla have famously delivered massive worlds with main quests that could have players spending 50 hours or more just to complete the story. For Fable, that won't be the case, but longtime fans probably expected that.

Howlongtobeat has the original 2004 Fable 's main quest clocking in at about 12 and a half hours. Fable 2 isn't much longer at 13 hours , and Fable 3 inches just further past that at 13 and a half hours . If anything, next year's Fable reboot is already shaping up to be the longest in the series, and pushing its main campaign on much longer would have it launching with a story almost twice as long as the one in the original game.

That's not to say that players won't be able to get lost in Fable's fantasy world if they so choose. Kennedy promised that the new Fable game's "life systems are limitless, so you can play them for as long as you want." When one attendee remarked that Fable is "not a huge game," Littler clarified, again, that "you can literally play it forever if that's what you want to do."

Compared to the rest of the series, completionists will typically spend about 30 hours seeing all there is to see in the first game and around 50 to do the same in the second and third games. The next Fable appears to be fall in line with that trend, but we won't truly see all it has to offer until Playground and Xbox see it launch next year.

Fable is currently set with a February 23, 2027, release date for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. IGN got to see one of its full quests in action at gamescom 2026 and came away even more excited to see what the full game has to offer. After first being announced six years ago in July 2020, director Ralph Fulton tells us he's happy to see it launch alongside a bunch of other games and relieved that Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't one of them .

articles.title: Star Wars and Jurassic Park VFX Legend Phil Tippett Closes Studio and Auctions Memorabilia
articles.summary: Oscar-winning animator Phil Tippett is closing his Berkeley studio and auctioning off legendary Star Wars, Jurassic Park, and RoboCop props and memorabilia.
articles.body:
Phil Tippett – the Oscar-winning animator and visual effects supervisor whose dazzling stop-motion animation work appears in the original Star Wars trilogy , 1987’s RoboCop , and Jurassic Park – has announced the closure of his Berkeley, California studio.

Tippett, 74, sold his work – including memorabilia and props – at a two-day auction held this weekend , the artist informed the Berkeleyside news site (via FilmStories ).

The items auctioned at the liquidation sale – the result of Tippett Studio’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy – included stop-motion models of AT-ATs from Empire Strikes Back , autographed posters from Jurassic World and The Mandalorian, and much more ( click here to view the full gallery of Tippett’s collection).

“I’m retired from the racket,” Tippett said. “My last major project was the Twilight series. ”

The pioneering animator was inspired to pursue a career in stop-motion animation after seeing Ray Harryhausen's The 7th Voyage of Sinbad as a child.

During his four-decade-long film career, Tippett worked for Industrial Light & Magic on the Dejarik game scene in Star Wars: A New Hope, 1981’s Dragonslayer, and 1983’s Return of the Jedi, which won Tippett his first Academy Award for visual effects. He also won for Jurassic Park.

“I’m keeping the Oscars,” Tippett told Berkeleyside.

Phil Tippett’s other film credits include Starship Troopers, The Haunting, Dragonheart, Willow, Howard the Duck, RoboCop 2, and the 2021 film Mad God , which Tippett also directed.

articles.title: Ridley Scott's The Dog Stars Bombs in Theaters With $19 Million Global Opening
articles.summary: Ridley Scott's The Dogs Stars bombed at the box office in its first weekend in theaters with an estimated global opening of $19.3 million.
articles.body:
Ridley Scott's The Dogs Stars bombed at the box office in its first weekend in theaters with an estimated global opening of $19.3 million.

It was a rough debut for the Disney and 20th Century Studios picture, which brought Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, and Josh Brolin to cinemas with their live-action adaptation of Peter Heller's 2012 novel. In the first few days since its August 28, 2026, premiere, Scott's film only managed to land in sixth at the worldwide box office with a disappointing $8 million across 3,330 domestic locations and $11.3 million internationally.

"Ridley Scott’s The Dog Stars is a riveting, epic thriller set in a world where survival is instinct, but humanity is a choice," an official synopsis said. "Scott tells the story of Hig (Elordi), a young pilot who, together with a military survivalist, Bangley (Brolin), has carved out an efficient but isolated homestead in a brutal post-apocalyptic world until a mysterious radio transmission spurs Hig to venture into the unknown in search of the hope and humanity he still believes exists."

There are a number of factors that could have contributed to a soft launch for The Dog Stars despite featuring more than a few notable actors in its cast. Reviews, for example, have not landed in its favor.

Review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes recorded a "rotten" 41% favorability rating. IGN's review fell into a similar camp, delivering a 5/10 for Scott's latest. In our piece, we called it "a post-apocalyptic survival story that’s encased in three layers of emotionally protective bubble wrap with a wild third-act twist.

Audience scores for the film are much higher at 70%. However, that seems to have done little to convince moviegoers to head to theaters to see Elordi and Qualley on the big screen. With Variety reporting it had an $80 million budget, The Dog Stars has a lot of walking to do before it can even sniff at the idea of turning a profit.

The Dog Stars wasn't the only film making its theatrical debut in the late-August weekend. Coyote vs. Acme made its grand entrance when Ketchup Entertainment brought its wide release to theaters with a domestic haul of $15.46 million and an international haul of $8.42 million ($23.89 million global), proving that campaigners were willing to show up for the movie they've been fighting for. The film's Looney Tunes-mixed David and Goliath story nearly saw it permanently shelved at Warner Bros. before Ketchup – as well as a horde of online movie fans – swooped in to push for its release.

Now, we're here, and after landing in second place at the domestic box office and fifth globally, it seems to have all been worth it. Starring Will Forte, Lana Condor, and John Cena, reviews for the cartoons-come-to-life tale have generally been strong, with IGN calling it "amazing" in our 9/10 review .

pic.twitter.com/CEXEs5Pqux — Dave Green (@dgreenmachine) August 28, 2026

"Coyote vs. Acme shows why Looney Tunes are just as funny now as they’ve ever been," we said, "with a film that’s an amazingly meta answer to corporate shenanigans."

You can probably guess most of the other films that landed in the top five for the global box office. Spider-Man: Brand New Day finished its first month in theaters atop the box office charts once again, with its global total now at a spectacular $2.332 billion. The Odyssey continued its charge, too, coming in second with its worldwide total now at $1.552 billion. In third was Insidious: Out of the Further , which reached $110.2 million in its second weekend, and in fourth was Once Upon a Time in the Middle East, which has a total of $289 million.

September 2026 isn't quite set up for the bombshell box office returns we saw in July and August, but that doesn't mean there won't be a good reason to head to movies. Projects like Practical Magic 2 , Runner, Oasis reunion documentary Don't Look Back in Anger, and The Uprising are just days away from their respective premieres. Heavy hitters like Primtime , Zach Cregger's Resident Evil , and Marvel's Avengers: Endgame re-release are also due out before the end of the month.

articles.title: GTA 5's Michael Actor Defends GTA 6 After Doubters Say Rockstar's Games Look Too Similar
articles.summary: Ned Luke, the actor behind Grand Theft Auto 5's Michael De Santa, said people who think Grand Theft Auto 6 looks too much like GTA 5 are "out of their minds."
articles.body:
Ned Luke, the actor behind Grand Theft Auto 5 's Michael De Santa, said people who think Grand Theft Auto 6 looks too much like GTA 5 are "out of their minds."

Luke has remained an important figure in the GTA community since he first appeared as one of three playable professional criminals in the 2013 installment. Now that he and the rest of the world have gotten a closer look at what Rockstar Games is cooking up with GTA 6, he's stepped in to defend it from the naysayers.

One of the many, many talking points to emerge in the wake of last week's GTA 6: Extended Look was that playing as protagonists Jason and Lucia looked a little too similar to the kind of gameplay one could expect from GTA 5. While most seem to believe Rockstar has wisely used the 13 years since that game's release, it hasn't stopped skepticism from creeping in.

Luke doesn't seem to be included in the new game's cast, but he still made sure to refute some of the criticisms popping up online while collaborating with YouTube channels Partychat and House of Highlights . When asked for his thoughts about those who believe there are too many similarities between GTA 5 and GTA 6, he made his stance clear.

"This looks nothing like Grand Theft Auto 5," he said. "I think they're out of their minds."

"I'll tell you one thing: I never looked that good," he added, pointing to an image of Jason on his screen."

Rockstar's GTA 6 extended look officially revealed footage of a host of new features, including tons of new side activities , story missions , a reworked Wanted system , and more. For Luke, one of the best examples of how Rockstar has reimagined Grand Theft Auto can be seen in how its many characters move.

Thank you Ned Luke pic.twitter.com/FozLjRVSML — Zay 🔜 SWCLA (@justxavierisunc) August 30, 2026

Thank you Ned Luke pic.twitter.com/FozLjRVSML

"Watch the way the people move," he continued. "The walks are actual human walks. We still had a little bit of that mechanical thing going with our walks and the way we'd stand. For me, I felt like my legs were never fully straight. They always had this little bend in them."

He continued: "The technology has grown by leaps and bounds, you know? What would make you think it's going to be better than those games? It's no diss to those games. It's like between [GTA 5] and GTA 4. Our graphics blew GTA 4 away. They weren't even close."

Luke then called attention to the high level of detail in the planes, helicopters, and car explosions shown through the extended look. He even went as far as to address the comments saying GTA 6 didn't look much better than 2018's Red Dead Redemption 2, saying, "Sorry, guys, you're wrong. The graphics here beat Red Dead."

The actor behind GTA's Michael has stayed in touch with Rockstar fans in the years since his debut and has been known to speak his mind . In 2024, for example, he praised Lucia's introduction in GTA 6 as "huge."

"Lucia's hard, man," he said at the time. "In the trailer, she looked good. You get a lot of these clowns out here going, 'Rockstar's going woke, they're caving into the wokeness of the world,'" Luke said. "First of all, there's been other female protagonists in the past, but not in something as huge as this."

GTA 6 is scheduled to come to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. While its extended look on Netflix gave fans a lot to chew on, Rockstar still has plenty more to show between now and then. While we wait, you can check out all of IGN's exclusive coverage, including our preview and interview . There's also our list of 99 details we caught during the extended look and the 69 details we saw at Rockstar HQ .
